support_body.geometric_claim: A distinguishable circular bearing seat or carrier recess is visibly formed within a surrounding support body; a generic unfeatured through-bore alone is ambiguous.
Holes, slots or feet suitable as attachment geometry are visible on that same surrounding carrier.
The seat is carried by the same rigid body that bears the mounting interface, rather than by a separate shaft or loose bearing ring.
The surrounding body has a nonrotating carrier/housing form beyond a plain rotating ring, wheel or generic pipe-flange disk.

shaft_connector.geometric_claim: Two distinct shaft-receiving ends are visible on the body; they may be coaxial or mechanically articulated. An unfeatured pipe bore alone is ambiguous.
A keyway, spline, clamp split, tightening screw arrangement or equivalent positive shaft attachment is visible at the first receiving end.
A keyway, spline, clamp split, tightening screw arrangement or equivalent positive shaft attachment is visible at the other receiving end.
The two shaft attachment regions are visibly joined by a continuous rigid, flexible or articulated mechanical connection body.

belt_wheel.geometric_claim: A substantially circular wheel rim is visible about a rotation axis.
A circumferential belt-contact track is visible: a continuous belt groove, V-channel, or timing-belt-like repeated tooth band.
The track has identifiable belt guidance/profile geometry (groove flanks, edge flanges, or belt-type transverse teeth), rather than an unqualified gear-tooth pattern.
The identified belt-contact profile extends circumferentially around the same wheel rim, rather than appearing on an unrelated component.

threaded_clamp.geometric_claim: A head and a shank are connected as one fastener-shaped body; short headed screws also qualify.
An underside bearing surface on the head is visible around the shank.
A helical external thread is visibly modeled on the shank; a smooth cylinder alone is not positive evidence.
The head has a turning/drive feature such as wrench flats, socket, slot or recess on the same body.

nut_retention.geometric_claim: A standalone compact body with an axial bore is visible, rather than an externally threaded bolt or long sleeve.
External flats, wings, notches or another explicit turning feature are visible on that bored body.
An internal helical thread is visibly modeled inside the bore; an untextured hole alone is not positive evidence.
The internally threaded bore and the external turning interface belong to the same compact body.

bracket_mount.geometric_claim: Two distinct orthogonal, angled or offset attachment face regions are visibly present on one structural body.
The two regions are rigidly joined, rather than linked by an articulating hinge pin.
A mounting hole or slot lies on the first attachment region.
A mounting hole or slot lies on the other attachment region; it must not be the same hole counted twice.

flanged_passage.geometric_claim: A central through-passage is visibly open through the body; a blind pocket is insufficient.
Several peripheral mounting holes form a pattern around that same central passage.
A flat annular mating-face region surrounds the passage and is associated with the peripheral bolt pattern.
A raised or recessed coaxial mating register/neck is visibly formed around the passage on the same body.

gear_mesh.geometric_claim: A cylindrical wheel or local cylindrical gear band integral with a shaft is visible about a rotation axis, rather than only a conical bevel or worm form.
Repeated projecting teeth are visible on the outer circumference of that wheel.
The tooth geometry visibly has spur or helical gear form; ambiguous fine timing-belt teeth alone are insufficient.
The teeth form an exposed circumferential meshing band on the cylindrical wheel, rather than being confined as fine belt teeth between belt flanges.

shaft_drive.geometric_claim: An elongated, predominantly axial solid/journal-like body is visible rather than a short hollow hub.
Cylindrical journal or stepped shaft regions lie along the same elongated body.
A keyway, spline, integral gear, crank/eccentric or noncircular drive feature is visibly formed on the body; simple shoulders or screw threads alone are insufficient.
The visible form is a rotary drive body rather than a headed fastening screw or a thread-only linear screw.

compression_return.geometric_claim: A helical wire coil body is visibly present rather than a solid threaded rod or flat clip.
Axial gaps between multiple adjacent turns are visible, providing geometric coil travel.
Both terminal regions terminate as axial seating ends of that coil rather than extension hooks or long torsion arms.
The same coil has no terminal extension hooks/loops or projecting torsion arms; assert yes only when both terminal regions are visible.

tension_return.geometric_claim: A helical wire coil body is visibly present rather than a solid threaded rod or flat clip.
A terminal hook or loop is visibly attached to one end of that coil; a straight torsion arm alone does not qualify.
A second terminal hook or loop is visibly attached to the other end of the same coil.
The two hooks/loops are bound to opposite axial ends of the same coil to form two tensile attachment regions, rather than unrelated loops or torsion arms.
